titulo: Weekly Test 4 — Comparing texts, fact and opinion, present perfect and conjunctions

bloques.html: Instructions: Read each question carefully. For multiple-choice questions, mark the letter of the correct answer with an ✗. Write complete sentences when there are lines. We start with Listening: an adult will read a short podcast aloud twice.

Adulto: el guion está en la pauta. Léelo en voz alta dos veces, a ritmo normal, con una pausa de 30 segundos entre lecturas. 1 punto cada una.

Listen to the podcast "Who Invented the Bicycle?" and answer questions 1 to 5.
What was the first bicycle made of? (1 pt)

alternativas.html: By pushing with his feet on the ground

bloques.html: How did the rider move the "dandy horse"? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: C) By pushing with his feet on the ground

alternativas.html: The rider could fly over the handlebars if the wheel hit a stone.

bloques.html: Why were the bicycles with a giant front wheel dangerous? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) The rider could fly over the handlebars if the wheel hit a stone

alternativas.html: Two wheels of the same size, a chain and pedals

bloques.html: What did the "safety bicycle" have that modern bikes also have? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) Two wheels of the same size, a chain and pedals

alternativas.html: Because it was slower than the other bikes
Because riders did not fall over the front wheel, so it was safer than the giant-wheel bike
Because it was made in a safe factory

bloques.html: Why do you think it was called the "safety bicycle"? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: C) Because riders did not fall over the front wheel, so it was safer

bloques.html:
Read both texts and answer questions 6 to 11.

Text A: Temuco Opens New Bike Lanes (from a local newspaper)

Last Monday, the city of Temuco opened eight kilometers of new bike lanes connecting three neighborhoods with the center. The lanes are painted green and separated from cars by a low concrete curb. According to the city, more than 2,000 people have already used them in the first week. The mayor said the project cost 1.2 billion pesos and took ten months to build. Some drivers have complained that the lanes removed parking spaces on two streets. The city plans to add another five kilometers next year, including a route to the university. Bike shops near the new lanes report that sales of helmets and lights have increased since the opening.

Text B: Letter to the principal

Dear Ms. Rojas,
I am writing to ask you to build a bike rack at our school. Since the new lanes opened, I have ridden my bike to school every day, and it is the best part of my morning. Riding is healthier than sitting in a car, and it does not pollute. However, there is nowhere safe to leave our bikes. Last week, two students had to lock their bikes to the fence, and a teacher asked them to move. I think at least thirty students would ride if they had a place to park. A bike rack is not expensive, and it would make our school greener and happier. I hope you will consider my idea.
Sincerely, Daniela, Grade 5

alternativas.html: To persuade people to ride bikes
To inform readers about the new bike lanes

bloques.html: What is the author's purpose in Text A? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) To inform readers about the new bike lanes
pauta.oa: CCSS RI.5.6 / RI.5.8 — propósito del autor

alternativas.html: To inform about the cost of the lanes
To persuade the principal to build a bike rack

bloques.html: What is Daniela's purpose in Text B? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) To persuade the principal to build a bike rack

alternativas.html: It is the best part of my morning.
Two students locked their bikes to the fence.

bloques.html: Which sentence is an opinion? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: C) It is the best part of my morning

alternativas.html: Bike lanes are a great idea.
More than 2,000 people used the lanes in the first week.

bloques.html: Which sentence is a fact from Text A? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: B) More than 2,000 people used the lanes in the first week

alternativas.html: A bike rack at the school
A problem about where to park or leave bikes or cars

bloques.html: What do both texts mention? (1 pt)

pauta.respuesta: D) A problem about where to park or leave bikes or cars (A: se perdieron estacionamientos; B: no hay dónde dejar las bicicletas)
pauta.oa: RI.5.9 — integrar información de dos textos

bloques.html: How are the two texts different in the way they are written? Give one clear difference (think about who is speaking and what kind of information each text gives). (2 pts)

pauta.respuesta: 2 pts: nombra una diferencia clara y la apoya con ambos textos; p. ej. "Text A is a news report in third person that gives facts and numbers; Text B is a letter in first person that gives Daniela's opinion and asks for something". 1 pt: diferencia correcta pero vaga o solo sobre un texto ("B is a letter"). 0: diferencia falsa o solo de contenido ("A talks about lanes, B about a rack")
pauta.oa: RI.5.6 / RI.5.9 — comparar punto de vista y tipo de texto

bloques.html: Choose the correct form: Daniela her bike to school every day since the lanes opened. (1 pt)

pauta.oa: OA14-16 / CCSS L.5.1 — presente perfecto con *since*

alternativas.html: I have never saw a bike rack at our school.
I have never seen a bike rack at our school.
I never have see a bike rack at our school.
I has never seen a bike rack at our school.

bloques.html: Which sentence is correct? (1 pt)
Choose the best conjunction: Riding a bike is healthy, there is nowhere to park. (1 pt)

Join each pair of sentences using one conjunction from the box. Use a different conjunction each time. (2 pts)

because   ·   although   ·   so

a) The city removed parking spaces. Some drivers complained.

b) It was raining. Daniela rode her bike.

pauta.respuesta: a) "The city removed parking spaces, so some drivers complained." o "Some drivers complained because the city removed parking spaces." b) "Although it was raining, Daniela rode her bike." (o "Daniela rode her bike although it was raining"). 1 pt cada una; la conjunción debe tener sentido lógico y ser distinta en a) y b). Aceptar "because" en a) si usó "although" en b)

bloques.html: Write an opinion paragraph of 6 to 7 sentences: Should students be allowed to ride bikes or scooters to school? State your opinion, give two reasons with examples, and finish with a conclusion. Use at least two conjunctions. (5 pts)

pauta.respuesta: Rúbrica de escritura (5 criterios × 1 pt), ver abajo

Talk with the adult: give your opinion with reasons and tell a story. (8 pts)

pauta.oa: OA10-13 / Flyers Speaking — opinar y narrar

pautaHtml:
Guion de Listening (leer dos veces, en voz alta)

Lee a ritmo normal, como un podcast. Pausa de 30 segundos entre lecturas. No expliques palabras.

Who Invented the Bicycle?

Have you ever wondered who invented the bicycle? The first one appeared in Germany in 1817. It was made of wood and had no pedals. The rider sat on it and pushed with his feet along the ground, like a running machine. People called it the "dandy horse".

Pedals arrived about fifty years later, in France. But those bikes had a giant front wheel, sometimes taller than a man, and a tiny back wheel. They were fast but very dangerous: if the front wheel hit a stone, the rider flew over the handlebars.

In 1885, an English inventor built the "safety bicycle". It had two wheels of the same size, a chain, and pedals in the middle, almost exactly like the bikes we ride today. A few years later, rubber tires filled with air made the ride soft and quiet.

Since then, the bicycle has changed very little. Scientists say it is still the most efficient machine ever built for moving a person: nothing else goes so far using so little energy.

Guion de Speaking (4-5 minutos)

Solo en inglés. No corrijas durante la conversación; anota y califica al final.

  1. Warm-up (30 s, no se califica): "Hi! Have you ever ridden a bike to school? How was it?"
  2. Opinion (2 min): "Some people think it's better to read a book; others prefer to watch the movie. What do you think, and why? Give me two reasons." Apoyo: "Can you give me an example?" / "What would someone who disagrees with you say?"
  3. Story (2 min): "Tell me about a time you changed your mind about something. What did you think at first, what happened, and what did you think at the end?" Apoyo: "Why did you change your mind?" / "How did it end?"
  4. Cierre: "Thank you, that's all."

Rúbricas

Escritura (ítem 16) — 1 punto por criterio cumplido:

Criterio 1 pt si...
Opinión clara La primera o segunda oración dice claramente qué piensa (I think / In my opinion / Students should...)
Razones Da dos razones distintas y al menos una con ejemplo o explicación
Organización Opinión → razones → conclusión; usa conectores (first, second, because, so, for these reasons); 6-7 oraciones
Gramática Al menos dos conjunciones bien usadas; máximo 2 errores gramaticales
Ortografía y puntuación Mayúsculas y puntos en todas las oraciones; máximo 2 errores de ortografía

Speaking (ítem 17) — cada criterio 0, 1 o 2 puntos:

Criterio 2 pts 1 pt 0 pts
Contenido Opinión con dos razones y un ejemplo; historia completa con el cambio de opinión explicado Una razón o historia incompleta Respuestas mínimas o no responde
Organización Ideas en orden con conectores (first, because, but, at first, then, in the end) Orden confuso o sin conectores Sin estructura
Vocabulario Variado y preciso; usa expresiones de opinión (I think, I believe, in my opinion, I agree) Repite palabras básicas o cambia a español en 1-2 palabras Muy limitado; mezcla español con frecuencia
Corrección Tiempos verbales (pasado, presente perfecto) y concordancia correctos casi siempre (máximo 2 errores) Varios errores que no impiden entender Errores constantes que dificultan entender

Qué mira este instrumento

Fase B→C. Comprensión auditiva de un texto informativo-histórico con inferencia (1-5); lectura comparada de dos textos sobre el mismo tema: propósito del autor, hecho vs. opinión, integración de información (6-11), al nivel CCSS RI.5.6-RI.5.9; presente perfecto y conjunciones (12-15); párrafo de opinión con razones (16); speaking de opinión y narración (17).

Señales: si falla 6-7, no distingue aún para qué se escribe un texto (informar / persuadir); eso se trabaja preguntando "¿qué quiere el autor que yo haga o piense?". Si falla 8-9, confunde hecho con opinión: pedirle que pregunte "¿se puede comprobar?". Si 11 saca 0-1, compara contenido pero no forma; es una habilidad de techo (RI.5.9) y es normal que esté en construcción. Si 12-13 fallan, el presente perfecto no está automatizado por escrito; verificar si lo usa bien al hablar (si sí, es forma; si no, es gramática real).

Si le fue mal

  • Propósito del autor: con cada texto que lea en la semana (noticia, aviso, cuento, carta), decir en una palabra "inform / persuade / entertain" y por qué.
  • Hecho vs. opinión: juego de 10 frases dichas por el adulto; el niño grita "fact" u "opinion" y explica cómo se podría comprobar.
  • Presente perfecto: preguntas diarias "Have you ever...?" y "How long have you...?" y exigir respuesta completa con have/has + participio.
  • Conjunciones: dar dos oraciones sueltas y pedir que las una con "because", luego con "so", luego con "although", notando cómo cambia el sentido.
  • Párrafo de opinión: usar la plantilla de la guía (opinión, razón 1 + ejemplo, razón 2 + ejemplo, conclusión) para escribir sobre un tema que le importe.
